match.reason: None of the bank points teaches standing waves; they cover matter waves, Maxwell's electromagnetic waves, the electromagnetic spectrum and Young's double slit interference, so the standing wave idea needs a new point.

draft.title: Standing waves
card: A wave that meets a boundary is reflected. The incoming wave and the reflected wave travel in opposite directions and add together as they overlap.
a point that stays still, because the two waves always arrive opposite and cancel there. Nodes are fixed in place.
a point where the two waves always arrive together and add, so the medium moves with the largest amplitude. Antinodes are also fixed in place.

The pattern does not travel along the medium, which is why it is called a standing wave. Neighbouring nodes are half a wavelength apart, and a node and the next antinode are a quarter of a wavelength apart.
draft.remember: A wave plus its reflection gives a standing wave: fixed nodes of no movement and fixed antinodes of largest movement.

a.q: A guitar string is plucked and a standing wave forms on it. What is true of a node on the string?
opts: It stays still because the two waves cancel there
It moves most because the two waves add there
It moves along the string at the wave speed
It stays still because no wave reaches it
a.why: At a node the incoming and reflected waves always arrive opposite, so they cancel and the string does not move. The tempting last option is wrong because both waves do reach the node. It is the cancelling that keeps it still.
a.clue: Think about what the two waves do when they arrive opposite.

b.q: A standing wave forms on a rope with a wavelength of 1.2 m. What is the distance from one node to the next antinode?
b.why: Neighbouring nodes are half a wavelength apart, which is 0.60 m. An antinode sits midway between two nodes, so a node and the next antinode are a quarter of a wavelength apart: 1.2 ÷ 4 = 0.30 m. The tempting 0.60 m is the distance from node to node.
b.clue: An antinode lies halfway between two neighbouring nodes.

a.best: It stays still because the two waves cancel there

problems.detail: The why calls 'the tempting last option' the one that is wrong 'because both waves do reach the node', meaning 'It stays still because no wave reaches it'. The options are shuffled, so that option is not last here, and the last option shown is 'It moves along the string at the wave speed'. Name the option by its wording, not its position.

check.summary: The card and both questions are correct, and each question has one clear right answer (a: the node stays still because the waves cancel; b: 0.30 m). The only issue is that the why for (a) refers to 'the last option', which does not match the shuffled order. It should name the option by its wording.
